answer: Plants rely on a special upward-pointing organ called the root cap, which contains tiny hairs that detect gravity directly, giving the plant a clear compass point. Once the cap senses gravity, it starts to grow faster toward it, lifting the entire shoot upwards as if walking hand over hand. So every shoot and root on a plant is automatically oriented with the root cap as a built-in compass needle, ensuring all parts are angled exactly west to east and point toward true north.
